![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/f5b69213924ffd4f7aef6acf1837fd05fbf6b0fd684de12a19f067e452fe42ea.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $y=x$ and $y=\frac{{x}^{3}}{4},$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $f(x)=x$ and $g(x)=\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ x & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{4} \\ 4x-{x}^{3} & =0 \\ x(4-{x}^{2}) & =0 \\ x(2-x)(2+x) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0,$ $x=-2,$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2$ because we are only concerned about $x\ge 0.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/ccbaa663f6f108322f7bafd4a192a5b9acdf913b61b8319048e92b7885458a91.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=\frac{{x}^{3}}{4},$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=x.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x([x]-[\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(4{x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
